# counts per member per year 

```{r}
#| label: correlations-deciles-across-types-years
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| layout-ncol: 1
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)


# 1. Load and summarize each type
counts <- map_dfr(1:5, function(type_id) {

  # Load into a separate environment to avoid overwriting objects
  env <- new.env()
  load(
    here::here("data", as.character(type_id), "data_member.rda"),
    envir = env
  )

  env$data_member |>
    filter(year > 2006, year < 2018) |>
    group_by(icpsr, chamber, year) |>
    summarise(
      perYear_sum = sum(perYear),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      type = type_id,
      perYear_decile = ntile(perYear_sum, 10)
    )
})

# 2. Calculate correlations between decile indicators for each type pair
type_pairs <- combn(1:5, 2, simplify = FALSE)

decile_correlations <- map_dfr(type_pairs, function(pair) {

  type_a <- pair[1]
  type_b <- pair[2]

  a <- counts |>
    filter(type == type_a) |>
    select(icpsr, chamber, year, decile_a = perYear_decile)

  b <- counts |>
    filter(type == type_b) |>
    select(icpsr, chamber, year, decile_b = perYear_decile)

  matched <- inner_join(
    a, b,
    by = c("icpsr", "chamber", "year")
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(decile_a), !is.na(decile_b))

  # One binary indicator column per decile
  indicators_a <- outer(matched$decile_a, 1:10, `==`) * 1
  indicators_b <- outer(matched$decile_b, 1:10, `==`) * 1

  # Correlation is undefined if either indicator has zero variance
  correlations <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 10, ncol = 10)

  if (nrow(matched) >= 2) {
    valid_a <- apply(indicators_a, 2, sd) > 0
    valid_b <- apply(indicators_b, 2, sd) > 0

    if (any(valid_a) && any(valid_b)) {
      correlations[valid_a, valid_b] <- cor(
        indicators_a[, valid_a, drop = FALSE],
        indicators_b[, valid_b, drop = FALSE]
      )
    }
  }

  # expand_grid varies decile_b fastest; transpose before flattening
  expand_grid(
    decile_a = 1:10,
    decile_b = 1:10
  ) |>
    mutate(
      correlation = as.vector(t(correlations)),
      comparison = paste("Type", type_a, "vs. Type", type_b),
      n_matched = nrow(matched)
    )
})

decile_correlations <- decile_correlations |>
  mutate(
    # For binary indicators, n * r^2 is the Pearson chi-squared
    # statistic for the corresponding 2 × 2 table.
    p_value = pchisq(
      n_matched * correlation^2,
      df = 1,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    ),
    p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significance = case_when(
      !is.na(p_adjusted) & p_adjusted < 0.05 & correlation > 0 ~ "+",
      !is.na(p_adjusted) & p_adjusted < 0.05 & correlation < 0 ~ "-",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

# 3. Plot all 10 unique type comparisons
ggplot(
  decile_correlations,
  aes(x = decile_b, y = decile_a, fill = correlation)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
geom_text(
  aes(label = significance),
  color = "black",
  #size = 4,
  fontface = "bold"
) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    #limits = c(-1, 1),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Correlation"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Decile within chamber",
    y = "Decile within chamber",
    title = "Correlations across types",
    subtitle = "Matched by member, chamber, and year",
    caption = paste(
  "+ / -: χ² test correlation with BH-adjusted p < 0.05."
  ) )  +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```




# correlations per congress 


```{r}
#| label: correlations-deciles-across-types
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| layout-ncol: 1
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)


# 1. Load and summarize each type
counts <- map_dfr(1:5, function(type_id) {

  # Load into a separate environment to avoid overwriting objects
  env <- new.env()
  load(
    here::here("data", as.character(type_id), "data_member.rda"),
    envir = env
  )

  env$data_member |>
    filter(year > 2006, year < 2018) |>
    group_by(icpsr, chamber, congress) |>
    summarise(
      per_sum = sum(perYear),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      type = type_id,
      per_decile = ntile(per_sum, 10)
    )
})

# 2. Calculate correlations between decile indicators for each type pair
type_pairs <- combn(1:5, 2, simplify = FALSE)

decile_correlations <- map_dfr(type_pairs, function(pair) {

  type_a <- pair[1]
  type_b <- pair[2]

  a <- counts |>
    filter(type == type_a) |>
    select(icpsr, chamber, congress, decile_a = per_decile)

  b <- counts |>
    filter(type == type_b) |>
    select(icpsr, chamber, congress, decile_b = per_decile)

  matched <- inner_join(
    a, b,
    by = c("icpsr", "chamber", "congress")
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(decile_a), !is.na(decile_b))

  # One binary indicator column per decile
  indicators_a <- outer(matched$decile_a, 1:10, `==`) * 1
  indicators_b <- outer(matched$decile_b, 1:10, `==`) * 1

  # Correlation is undefined if either indicator has zero variance
  correlations <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 10, ncol = 10)

  if (nrow(matched) >= 2) {
    valid_a <- apply(indicators_a, 2, sd) > 0
    valid_b <- apply(indicators_b, 2, sd) > 0

    if (any(valid_a) && any(valid_b)) {
      correlations[valid_a, valid_b] <- cor(
        indicators_a[, valid_a, drop = FALSE],
        indicators_b[, valid_b, drop = FALSE]
      )
    }
  }

  # expand_grid varies decile_b fastest; transpose before flattening
  expand_grid(
    decile_a = 1:10,
    decile_b = 1:10
  ) |>
    mutate(
      correlation = as.vector(t(correlations)),
      comparison = paste("Type", type_a, "vs. Type", type_b),
      n_matched = nrow(matched)
    )
})

decile_correlations <- decile_correlations |>
  mutate(
    # For binary indicators, n * r^2 is the Pearson chi-squared
    # statistic for the corresponding 2 × 2 table.
    p_value = pchisq(
      n_matched * correlation^2,
      df = 1,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    ),
    p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significance = case_when(
      !is.na(p_adjusted) & p_adjusted < 0.05 & correlation > 0 ~ "+",
      !is.na(p_adjusted) & p_adjusted < 0.05 & correlation < 0 ~ "-",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

# 3. Plot all 10 unique type comparisons
# Prepare row/column type labels
pairs <- decile_correlations |>
  tidyr::extract(
    comparison,
    into = c("type_a", "type_b"),
    regex = "Type (\\d+) vs\\. Type (\\d+)",
    convert = TRUE,
    remove = FALSE
  )

# Mirror each comparison, swapping the decile axes as well
# Keep existing significance results; do not recalculate adjusted p-values
plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pairs,
  pairs |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      type_a = type_b,
      type_b = type_a,
      decile_a = decile_b,
      decile_b = decile_a,
      correlation,
      significance
    )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    type_a = factor(type_a, levels = 1:5, labels = paste("Type", 1:5)),
    type_b = factor(type_b, levels = 1:5, labels = paste("Type", 1:5))
  )

# Plot a type-by-type matrix; diagonal panels remain blank
ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = decile_b, y = decile_a, fill = correlation)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = significance),
    color = "black",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(type_a),
    cols = vars(type_b),
    switch = "both",
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#0072B2",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#D55E00",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Correlation"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Decile within chamber",
    y = "Decile within chamber",
    title = "Correlations across types",
    caption = paste(
      "+ / −: positive / negative correlation;",
      "χ² test with BH-adjusted p < 0.05."
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.5, "lines")
  )

# TRY 2 
library(patchwork)

# Extract the types for each comparison
plot_data <- decile_correlations |>
  tidyr::extract(
    comparison,
    into = c("type_a", "type_b"),
    regex = "Type (\\d+) vs\\. Type (\\d+)",
    convert = TRUE,
    remove = FALSE
  ) |> 
    mutate(Type_a = case_when(
            type_a == 1 ~ " Constituent (individual)",
            type_a == 2 ~ "Constituent (corporate)",
            type_a == 3 ~ "Constituent (nonprofit or \nlocal government)",
            type_a == 4 ~ "Policy (corporate)",
            type_a == 5 ~ "Policy (general)"
         ),
         Type_b = case_when(
            type_b == 1 ~ " Constituent (individual)",
            type_b == 2 ~ "Constituent (corporate)",
            type_b == 3 ~ "Constituent (nonprofit or \nlocal government)",
            type_b == 4 ~ "Policy (corporate)",
            type_b == 5 ~ "Policy (general)"
         )
         ) 

# Use a common color scale across all panels
fill_limit <- max(abs(plot_data$correlation), na.rm = TRUE)
if (!is.finite(fill_limit) || fill_limit == 0) fill_limit <- 1

# Make one plot per unique comparison
plots <- plot_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(type_a, type_b) |>
  dplyr::group_split() |>
  purrr::map(function(df) {
    ggplot(
      df,
      aes(x = decile_b, y = decile_a, fill = correlation)
    ) +
      geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = significance),
        color = "black",
        fontface = "bold"
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_fill_gradient2(
        low = "#0072B2",
        mid = "white",
        high = "#D55E00",
        midpoint = 0,
        limits = c(-.3, fill_limit),
        na.value = "grey80",
        name = "Correlation"
      ) +
      coord_equal() +
      labs(
        x = paste0("", df$Type_b[1], ""),
        y = paste0("", df$Type_a[1], "")
      ) +
      theme(
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
      )
  })

# Caption as a separate panel
caption_panel <- wrap_elements(
  full = grid::textGrob(
    paste(
      "+ / −: χ² test",
      "with BH-adjusted",
      "p < 0.05.",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    x = 0.05,
    y = 0.5,
    just = c("left", "center"),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10)
  )
)

# Ten plots + legend + caption = twelve cells
wrap_plots(
  c(plots, list(guide_area(), caption_panel)),
  ncol = 4,
  guides = "collect"
) +
  plot_annotation(
    #title = "Correlations across types"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.justification = "center"
  )
```


# counts per congress 



```{r}
#| label: correlations-deciles-across-types-counts
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
#| layout-ncol: 1

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

tile_counts <- purrr::map_dfr(
  combn(1:5, 2, simplify = FALSE),
  function(pair) {

    a <- counts |>
      dplyr::filter(type == pair[1]) |>
      dplyr::select(
        icpsr, chamber, congress,
        decile_a = per_decile
      )

    b <- counts |>
      dplyr::filter(type == pair[2]) |>
      dplyr::select(
        icpsr, chamber, congress,
        decile_b = per_decile
      )

    dplyr::inner_join(
      a, b,
      by = c("icpsr", "chamber", "congress")
    ) |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(decile_a), !is.na(decile_b)) |>
      dplyr::count(decile_a, decile_b, name = "tile_count") |>
      tidyr::complete(
        decile_a = 1:10,
        decile_b = 1:10,
        fill = list(tile_count = 0L)
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        type_a = pair[1],
        type_b = pair[2]
      )
  }
)

plot_data2 <- plot_data |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tile_counts,
    by = c("type_a", "type_b", "decile_a", "decile_b")
  )

# Shared scale across all ten plots
 count_limit <- max(plot_data2$tile_count, na.rm = TRUE)
 
 
# 2. Rebuild your plots with # count as the fillUse a sequential color scale because counts are nonnegative:
  
  
  plots <- plot_data2 |>
  dplyr::group_by(type_a, type_b) |>
  dplyr::group_split() |>
  purrr::map(function(df) {
    ggplot(
      df,
      aes(x = decile_b, y = decile_a, fill = tile_count)
    ) +
      geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = significance),
        color = "black",
        fontface = "bold"
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "white",
        high = "#D55E00",
        limits = c(0, count_limit),
        name = "Count"
      ) +
      coord_equal() +
labs(
  x = trimws(df$Type_b[1]),
  y = trimws(df$Type_a[1])
) + 
      theme(
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
      )
  })


# Caption as a separate panel
caption_panel <- wrap_elements(
  full = grid::textGrob(
    paste(
      "Deciles within each chamber within", 
      "a congress are based on the number",
      "of each type of request each member",
      "of Congress made to all federal agencies.",
      "Correlations (+ / −) indicate χ² test",
      "with a BH-adjusted p < 0.05.",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    x = 0.05,
    y = 0.5,
    just = c("left", "center"),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10)
  )
)

layout <- "
ABCD
EFGH
IJKK
"

wrap_plots(
  c(plots, list(caption_panel)),
  design = layout
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Correlations Across Types",
    subtitle = "by Decile within Chamber per Congress"
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
